registered: 2026-10-03, committed before any run on the real data
question: Does an LLM proposer, grounded in the vault notes, choose better lagged-return hypotheses than enumerating the whole grid or drawing K at random?

universe.caveat: SURVIVORSHIP-BIASED: 34 pairs still trading in 2026, each listed since 2020-01-01; KNCUSDT absent (fetch HTTP 404).

timing: delay 1: the signal at decision day t uses closes up to day t-1 only; the position is entered at the close of day t and held to the close of day t+1. Bars close at 23:59:59 UTC and the close is the execution mark, so available_delay_seconds is 0.
selection: Within each arm, the hypothesis with the highest validation mean rank IC; grid order (momentum before reversal, shorter lookback first) breaks ties. The test split never enters a selection.

llm.transport: local claude -p, tools disabled, recorded to apps/quantos/examples/loop/replay.real-2026-10.json
llm.eligible: every proposal the loop froze as a method card; the loop's own card rule and critic run unchanged
llm.on_failure: if claude fails, is logged out or returns 429, stop live calls, record why, and report the LLM arm as pending

grid.hypotheses: every signal x lookback in the grid (120)

costs.primary: rebalanced: one book held across days, traded daily back to the factor lab's unit-gross rank weights after drift; cost = 10 bps x traded notional, entry and final exit included
costs.conservative: sleeve: the factor lab's own model, every position opened and closed every day (also what the loop's card rule uses)

metrics: mean daily rank IC with its t-stat and one-sided p
mean daily net return per unit gross (rebalanced, and sleeve)
annualised Sharpe of daily net (x sqrt 365)
gate: Promote an arm's selection (and, in the LLM loop, a card awaiting the human gate) only if its test rebalanced net mean is > 0 AND > the highest test rebalanced net mean among the three baselines. The LLM arm's selection must also have passed the loop's card rule and critic. Applied by code; no discretionary human decision.

report: hypotheses tested on validation per arm and distinct overall
Bonferroni-adjusted validation p of each selection
deflated Sharpe (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) of each selection's validation daily IC series against its arm's trials
Holm-adjusted test p across the arms' selections
the per-hypothesis validation and test table

interpretation: A negative or null result is reported as such. The LLM may know 2024-2026 market history from pre-training, so an LLM win would be read as possible leakage, not skill, unless it survives a later period.
